maya: FYI nightly fused-attn run flagged a regression on the qkv-packed + bias+rope fused path. Perf numbers below, blown-out when seq_len >= 8192 :eyes:

maya: bench summary: model=llama-13b, seq=16384, batch=1, warm=3, iters=20
maya: before (commit c4f2a1): 1,120k tokens/s total; after (commit d9b4e7): 1,020k tokens/s ~9% drop

maya: command used:
```
./bench --model=llama-13b --kernel=fused_qkv_packed_bias_rope --seq=16384 --batch=1 --iters=20 --warmup=3
```

arjun: thanks — can you paste the commit range? suspect the merge that touched lane allocation and post-attn epilogue landed last night

maya: range: c4f2a1..d9b4e7 — main changes: lane allocator tweak + eager-epilogue fusion refactor (PR #8421)

li: microprofile flame from the failing run attached inline — attention_postproc (epilogue) CPU/GPU time jumped. top hotspots: epilogue_write (34%), qkv_pack (18%), kv_page_fault_handler (12%)

li: snippet of profiler event counts:
```
EpilogueWrite: 340K
QKVPack: 180K
KVPageFaults: 120K
BatcherIdleWait: 45K
```

sasha: interesting — KV page faults show up when seq > page_threshold. Could be prefetch heuristic regressed with new lane allocator (we changed prefetch distances). When pages thrash, epilogue spends time materializing paged KV into contiguous buffer which kills throughput

ben: can we toggle off epilogue fusion at runtime? if so we should A/B: fused vs unfused on canary to confirm impact. If unfused recovers perf then fusion ordering bug likely

maya: there is a feature flag: `ATTN_EPILOGUE_FUSION=1|0`. I ran quick toggles on the same commit d9b4e7:
- with fusion=1 -> 1,020k tok/s
- with fusion=0 -> 1,115k tok/s (back to baseline)

arjun: that's a smoking gun. But two possible causes: 1) fusion emits memory patterns that interact badly with paged KV prefetch, 2) fusion change introduced extra atomic ops in epilogue path causing stalls at high seq

theo: can we repro at smaller seq but multiple concurrent requests to stress batching heuristics? fused path might be sensitive to batch coalescing. Try seq=4096 x batch=4 to hit same tokens/step but different memory layout

maya: quick runs:
- seq=4096 batch=4 fusion=1 -> 1,060k tok/s
- seq=4096 batch=4 fusion=0 -> 1,080k tok/s (small gap)

li: microprofile flame for seq=4096 showed less KV page faults, but epilogue_write still +12% with fusion=1. Looks like fusion increases write amplification even without page faults

sasha: hypothesis: epilogue fusion introduces an extra copy to a fused output buffer so we miss write-combining. On top of that lane allocation change might have altered alignment and led to unaligned stores -> slower global memory writes. We should instrument for unaligned stores and L2 store throughput

ben: easy experiment: force 128B alignment in allocator and re-run fused path. If perf recovers then allocator alignment + fusion interaction is culprit

maya: scheduling: I'll run aligned-allocator branch + fusion=1 on nightly infra, and also run with epilogue fusion off for canary traffic. Will paste results here when done. ETA ~2 hours

ci-bot: perf/regress check started for run 2167891234. Job: nightly-fused-attn. Tests: microbench, batcher-smoke, kvcache-smoke

arjun: also add a short unit test to detect increase in KVPageFault counts per 10k tokens so we catch this earlier in CI. threshold tuning: <10 faults per 10k tokens

theo: note: fallback kernel path should be updated to prefer unfused kernel for seq>=8k until we fix this. That prevents customer-visible regressions quickly

sasha: agreed. I'll open PR to add runtime fallback policy: if seq >= 8192 && kv_page_faults_recent > 50 -> pick unfused kernel. quick patch + tests.

li: adding a micro-benchmark to our perf harness that toggles `ATTN_EPILOGUE_FUSION` across sequences/batches would catch regressions in future

maya: action items:
- maya: run aligned-allocator + fused job and post numbers (2h)
- sasha: PR for runtime fallback policy (today)
- arjun: add KVPageFault threshold test in perf CI (tomorrow)
- li: add micro-benchmark toggles to harness (this week)

ben: thanks team. if patches look small we can hotfix the unfused default until we root cause. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: perf/regress job 2167891234 update: failure on microbench (regression detected). See https://ci.redwood.internal/2167891234 for logs

maya: got the aligned-allocator run in: fused=1 + aligned -> 1,108k tok/s (almost baseline). preliminary conclusion: alignment + fusion interaction caused most of the drop. still small gap (~0.6%) but within noise

arjun: great signal. next step: bisect the allocator change to find offending commit and add alignment invariants to allocator tests. Also keep the runtime fallback until pr ships

sasha: I'll push the fallback PR and include a short comment in release notes about kernel selection for large sequences

maya: closing loop after we merge sasha's PR and the allocator test. thanks all.
